 Millions of Americans are due to receive their next Social Security payment this week, as the Social Security Administration (SSA) continues its November payment schedule. This week’s retirement benefits will be paid on Wednesday, November 18, to beneficiaries whose birthdays fall between the 11th and 20th of any month, according to the agency's official 2026 payment calendar. The amount each person receives varies considerably and depends on factors like their earnings during their entire working life and the age at which they began claiming retirement benefits. For example, the maximum retirement benefit for someone who starts claiming at age 70 in 2026 is $5,181 per month, although the SSA says that people can only qualify for that maximum if they earned the maximum taxable amount each year from age 22. Who Gets Paid This Week? The SSA generally divides retirement payments into three groups based on a beneficiary's date of birth. That means the November 18 payment is scheduled for beneficiaries with birthdays falling between the 11th and 20th. Some beneficiaries follow a different schedule. People who started receiving Social Security before May 1997, or who receive both Social Security and Supplemental Security Income (SSI), generally receive their Social Security benefit on the third of the month and their SSI on the first. The SSA says people who don’t receive their payment on time should wait three extra mailing days before contacting the agency. When Are the Remaining November Payments? One more Wednesday payment is scheduled after this week's checks. People with birthdays falling from the 21st through the 31st are set to receive their November Social Security payment on Wednesday, November 25. How Much Does Social Security Pay? There’s no single Social Security payment amount because retirement benefits are based partly on a person's earnings record. The SSA currently estimates that the average retired worker will be receiving around $2,094 a month by the end of December 2026, before the next Cost-Of-Living Adjustment (COLA) takes effect. At the top end, a worker who earned the highest amount counted by Social Security throughout their career and starts receiving benefits at age 70 in 2026 can receive $5,181 per month. For comparison, the maximum for somebody retiring at their full retirement age in 2026 is $4,152 per month, while the maximum for someone claiming at age 62 is $2,969. Those figures show why the age at which a person claims can make such a big difference. Social Security says retirement benefits can begin as early as age 62, but taking them before full retirement age reduces the monthly amount. Delaying benefits beyond full retirement age increases the payment until age 70. A New COLA Is Coming The payments arriving this week won’t include the newly announced 2027 COLA. Social Security and SSI benefits will rise by 3.6 percent in 2027, affecting around 76 million Americans. The higher payments will begin in January 2027 for nearly 72 million Social Security recipients, while increased payments for around 7.3 million SSI recipients will begin on December 31, 2026, with some eligible to receive both SSI and Social Security payments. The adjustment is designed to help benefits keep up with the rate of inflation, and is calculated using the Consumer Price Index (CPI) for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers, or CPI-W. For the average retired worker, the SSA estimates that the 3.6 percent COLA will increase a monthly benefit from about $2,094 to $2,170, a rise of roughly $76 a month. The increase will happen automatically, meaning beneficiaries don’t need to do anything to receive the higher amount.  Who Gets Paid This Week?
 ... The SSA generally divides retirement payments into three groups based on a beneficiary's date of birth .
 Those born from the 1st through the 10th are normally paid on the second Wednesday of the month. 
 People born from the 11th through the 20th receive their payment on the third Wednesday each month. 
 Those born from the 21st through the 31st are paid on the fourth Wednesday of every month.
 That means the November 18 payment is scheduled for beneficiaries with birthdays falling between the 11th and 20th.
 Some beneficiaries follow a different schedule. People who started receiving Social Security before May 1997, or who receive both Social Security and Supplemental Security Income (SSI), generally receive their Social Security benefit on the third of the month and their SSI on the first.

 One more Wednesday payment is scheduled after this week's checks.
 People with birthdays falling from the 21st through the 31st are set to receive their November Social Security payment on Wednesday, November 25.

 ... There’s no single Social Security payment amount because retirement benefits are based partly on a person's earnings record.
 The SSA currently estimates that the average retired worker will be receiving around $2,094 a month by the end of December 2026, before the next Cost-Of-Living Adjustment (COLA) takes effect.
 At the top end, a worker who earned the highest amount counted by Social Security throughout their career and starts receiving benefits at age 70 in 2026 can receive $5,181 per month.
 For comparison , the maximum for somebody retiring at their full retirement age in 2026 is $4,152 per month, while the maximum for someone claiming at age 62 is $2,969.
 Those figures show why the age at which a person claims can make such a big difference. Delaying benefits beyond full retirement age increases the payment until age 70.

 The payments arriving this week won’t include the newly announced 2027 COLA.
